WIDE CINEMATIC VISTA — establishing shot, eye-level horizon centered on lower third, sky and atmosphere fill upper two-thirds. Full depth visible from foreground to deep horizon. The kind of frame a film opens with.
EXTREME LOW ANGLE LOOKING UP — camera at ground level tilted upward, foreground tilted forward, sky filled with the impossible structure or formation. Forces vertical scale impression.
AERIAL SWEEP — high-altitude oblique, camera moving over the terrain, structures and landscape revealed from above. Helicopter-pull-back compositional energy.
LONG-LENS DEEP COMPRESSION — telephoto flattening layers, foreground / mid / deep all visible but stacked, atmospheric haze separating each depth band. Anchor entity is mid-distance silhouette.
WORM'S-EYE FROM RIDGE EDGE — foreground is a near cliff or terrace edge, midground falls away into the deep scene, far horizon glimpsed across the void. Vertigo composition.
OVER-THE-SHOULDER ANCHOR — anchor entity in foreground (back-turned), the wonder of the scene unfolding ahead of them. Caspar-Friedrich / Spielberg awe-pose.
DUTCH-TILT CHAOS — frame tilted 15-25 degrees, unsettled energy, used for THREAT or CONVERGENCE beats. Dramatic instability built into the composition.
BIRD'S-EYE TOP-DOWN — straight overhead view, the landscape reads as map-like, anchor entity is a tiny silhouette near center. Best for showing pattern and density.
SYMMETRIC HERO FRAME — anchor entity or structure centered on the vertical axis, environment symmetric to both sides, monumental balance. Used for ARRIVAL or VIGIL.
RACKED FOREGROUND — sharp tangible foreground element (railing, machinery, ruined stone) leading the eye into a soft-focus deep scene. Strong depth via focus contrast.
PROFILE PARALLAX — anchor entity in clean profile against a layered environment receding sideways, three depth bands visible (near terrain, mid-feature, far horizon).
BACKLIT SILHOUETTE — strong light source behind the anchor entity, scene rendered in heavy chiaroscuro, atmosphere visible in the light beam. Mood: sacred or threatening.
MIRRORED REFLECTION DUALITY — camera positioned to capture scene through reflective surface (water, glass, metal), real and reflected image split the frame creating symmetrical doubling of reality.
KEYHOLE VIEW PORTAL — camera shoots through narrow architectural gap or doorway in extreme foreground, framing distant sci-fi wonder as compressed focal point within geometric negative space.
TOP-DOWN CRANE PUSH-IN — descending vertical movement from high above, gradually tightening on central subject while maintaining perpendicular overhead perspective throughout the motion.
REVERSE-DOLLY REVEAL — camera pulls backward while subject remains static, progressively unveiling surrounding context and scale as frame widens to expose previously hidden environment.
FORCED PERSPECTIVE CORRIDOR — long telephoto lens compressing deep geometric hallway or canyon, flattening Z-axis distance into stacked layered planes of repeating architectural elements.

THROUGH-THE-GLASS SEPARATION — camera shoots through transparent barrier (window, force field, visor), creating visual layers with reflections, refractions, and dirt/condensation disrupting clean view of beyond.
CANTED HORIZON DRIFT — horizon line placed at steep diagonal angle, 30-45 degrees off level, creating disorientation while maintaining deep compositional thirds from corner to corner.

RACK-FOCUS SHIFT — shallow depth of field with focus pull transitioning attention from sharp foreground element to previously blurred background subject, recontextualizing the frame without camera movement.
SNORRICAM FACE-FORWARD — camera rigidly mounted facing subject's face while environment spins/moves behind them, locking viewer to character's perspective while world transforms around them.
BISECTED FRAME THRESHOLD — vertical or horizontal hard division splitting composition into two distinct environmental zones (light/dark, interior/exterior, tech/organic) with subject at the border.
WHIP-PAN BLUR TRANSITION — rapid horizontal camera swing creating motion-blurred streak across frame, implying speed, disorientation, or sudden temporal/spatial jump between story beats.
NEGATIVE SPACE ISOLATION — subject placed small within vast empty frame area, emphasizing loneliness and scale through compositional void rather than comparative environmental elements.
CIRCULAR VIGNETTE FOCUS — frame edges darkened or obscured in iris/tunnel effect, concentrating viewer attention to central circular area of clarity, suggesting POV limitation or optical device.

STEADICAM WEAVE FOLLOW — fluid tracking shot navigating through cluttered environment close behind moving subject, creating intimate pursuit energy while revealing spatial complexity through movement.
SPLIT-DIOPTER DUAL-FOCUS — specialized lens allowing simultaneous sharp focus on extreme foreground and deep background elements, creating hyper-real depth impossible to natural vision.
UPSIDE-DOWN INVERSION — camera rotated 180 degrees, presenting scene inverted with sky at bottom, creating cognitive dissonance and dreamlike destabilization of spatial logic.
CRASH-ZOOM PUNCH-IN — rapid focal length change driving lens from wide to tight telephoto on subject, aggressive attention-grabbing movement compressing space with visceral speed.
ORBITAL ARC ROTATION — camera circles subject at consistent radius, maintaining framing while background environment rotates around static central anchor, revealing 360-degree context.
FISH-EYE DISTORTION SPHERE — extreme wide-angle lens bending straight lines into curves, creating spherical warping that expands perceived space while distorting geometric reality.
LAYERED DEPTH PLANES — three or more distinct compositional layers stacked in Z-space (near/mid/far), each with separate action or visual interest, creating deep multi-focal complexity.
HANDHELD DOCUMENTARY SHAKE — intentional camera instability and micro-movements suggesting real-time human observation, trading polish for immediacy and chaotic naturalism.
SLOW-MOTION GLIDE — high frame-rate capture with lateral tracking movement, elongating time while smooth dolly creates dreamlike floating quality through otherwise static environment.
GEOMETRIC FRAME-WITHIN-FRAME — environmental architecture creates internal rectangular or shaped border within composition, nesting subject within multiple layers of visual containment.
EXTREME CLOSE MACRO DETAIL — lens positioned inches from surface texture or mechanical detail, abstracting larger object into landscape of tactile specificity and material reality.
HORIZON-BISECT SYMMETRY — perfectly level horizon line cutting frame exactly in half, mirroring compositional weight between ground and sky in formal balanced stability.
MIRRORED REFLECTION — camera captures scene through reflective surface (water, glass, metal hull), reality inverted or doubled, depth compressed into flat plane of reflection.
KEYHOLE VIEW — camera peers through narrow opening (doorway, porthole, cave mouth), frame-within-frame construction, deep focus from obscured foreground to distant revealed subject.
SPLIT-DIOPTER FOCUS — lens modification holds extreme foreground and distant background both in sharp focus, middle ground blurred, creates impossible depth compression.
WHIP-PAN TRANSITION — rapid horizontal camera movement blurs environment, snaps to halt on new subject or location, conveys speed and disorientation.
THROUGH-GLASS SEPARATION — camera shoots through transparent barrier (helmet visor, window, force field), layers subject behind protective surface, emphasizes isolation or containment.
FISHEYE DISTORTION — ultra-wide spherical lens warps straight lines into curves, exaggerates central subject, peripheral environment bends away into impossible geometry.
STEADICAM WEAVE — camera glides fluidly through environment at walking speed, threading between obstacles, creates immersive subjective movement without handheld shake.
PUSH-IN ZOOM HYBRID — simultaneous dolly-in and zoom-out (or reverse), background stretches or compresses while subject size remains constant, vertigo effect.
ORBITAL ROTATION — camera circles subject at constant radius, reveals all sides, subject remains centered while background environment sweeps past in continuous motion.

PRISMATIC SPLIT-FOCUS — lens or atmospheric distortion fragments the frame into overlapping angular panes, multiple focal planes simultaneously sharp, creates kaleidoscopic geometry around central anchor point.
KEYHOLE APERTURE — camera shoots through narrow circular or geometric opening in foreground structure, scene compressed into tunnel vision, vignette creates forbidden-glimpse tension.
SHATTERED GLASS MOSAIC — camera positioned behind fractured transparent barrier, scene fragmented into geometric shards, multiple focal planes create cubist simultaneity.

MIRRORED REFLECTION FRAME — camera positioned low to capture subject and environment reflected in still water, polished floor, or glossy surface, creating perfect symmetry between real and inverted world.
